purpose: Discriminate whether the approximately 44-minute coherent clock is more naturally interpreted as rotation/spin or binary/orbital modulation without allowing the favored model to redefine the test after inspection.
rotation_spin_hypothesis_predictions: A single coherent phase model should describe radio recurrence across epochs after barycentric and propagation corrections.
Pulse profile and polarization geometry should show repeatable rotational structure rather than eclipse-like orbital windows.
No companion radial-velocity, ellipsoidal, eclipse or orbital-heating signature is required.
Any radio-Xray phase offset should remain tied to rotational phase within uncertainties if both arise from a stable magnetospheric geometry.
The model must confront the difficulty of sustaining coherent radio emission at such a long rotation period rather than hiding it.
binary_orbital_hypothesis_predictions: Independent evidence should appear for a companion or orbital modulation: radial velocity, periodic optical/IR variation, eclipses, heating, accretion geometry, or timing delays.
The approximately 44-minute clock may remain coherent while pulse visibility or spectrum changes with orbital geometry.
A physically plausible component-density/Roche-lobe configuration must exist at the inferred orbital period.
Radio and Xray relative phase should have a stable orbital interpretation, or model-specific phase drift should be predicted quantitatively.
If orbital timing delays are measurable, adding binary parameters should improve timing residuals without unjustified extra freedom.
discriminating_observables: energy-budget consistency for neutron-star, magnetar and white-dwarf parameter spaces
